In this isometric view, we see a central cube with an orange face visible (the side face). The four arms extending out are blue. Actually, let's look. The top cube is blue. The left cube is blue. So the color configuration is the same: center orange, four arms blue. The shape is the same cross. So this is the same object, just rotated/viewed from a different angle.

Let's double check image 3 (Third): A cross shape rotated diagonally. Center = orange. Top-left arm = orange. Top-right arm = blue. Bottom-left arm = blue. Bottom-right arm = blue. So pattern: center orange, one arm orange, three arms blue. That's different from reference (all four arms blue). So Third is different.

Thus only the Second image matches.

Therefore the answer is B.

Let me double check the reference once more. Reference: top arm blue, left arm blue, right arm blue, bottom arm blue, center orange. Yes.

Second image: I see a top cube (blue), a left cube (blue), a right cube (blue), a bottom cube (blue), and center cube showing orange face. Yes matches.

The question: "Which of the following images is the same object as the previous image, if any?" The "previous image" is the first one shown (the reference cross with center orange and four blue arms). The following images are the three I analyzed. So answer = Second = B.
